newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/9.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.0/9.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 9.0/9.5 percent on Thursday morning on the back of flush supply in the money market, dealers said.
They said money rates were seen easing following central bank injection of some 461 billion rupiah, coupled with a central bank move to cut key SBPU discount rates by 50 basis points.
One-week money fell to 15.25 percent, two to 15.50 percent, one-, three-, six- and 12-month to 16.0 percent.
"The move does stimulate the market. But interest rates were already on a downtrend previously," one dealer said.
The dealer said the move did not have an immediate impact on the money market because interbank rates were trading much lower than the SBPU benchmarks.
However, it did cause pressure on longer-term forward premiums following the announcement, dealers said.
A bond dealer at Danareksa Sekuritas said the move caused the benchmark PLN V/A bond yield to fall by some 30 basis points on Thursday.
Short-dated swaps fell to 0.35/0.45 from 0.4/0.5 points on the back of relatively ample liquidity early in the morning.
